title: One index file over several data files
body:
An Index describes one file. Index::write stamps that file's length and mtime into the header. The free function is_current re-stats one data path against one index path. Aggregate<IndexedFasta> numbers several indexed files as one range. Nothing on disk records which files were aggregated or in which order. The numbering exists only in the call that built it. When one part's index is stale, sail rebuilds it in memory and says nothing.

This milestone adds a file for the aggregate: an ordered list of the parts with a stamp and a record count for each. One read of it gives the total and each part's first position. sail can name a changed part. sail index gains several inputs and an explicit -o to write one.

The pieces:

- sail-9d931d decides whether the file holds offsets or points at per-file .saidx files.
- sail-978552 decides what a stale part does.
- sail-f5a79d decides whether the file shares a version bump with the alignment work in sail-bb932e. It dissolves if sail-9d931d goes by reference, because the file then never touches the .saidx layout.
- sail-a59d6f is the type and its file.
- sail-2413e6 is the sail index command.

Alignment of the .saidx layout (sail-bb932e) left this milestone. It can be explained without the list file.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/c45d6630
notes.text: Split on 2026-10-12: this milestone was 'Selection over a stream and over several files, and an index that spans files' and mixed streaming with the index-file work. Streaming (sail-317db4) and the multi-file Reader (sail-0705fb, with its decision sail-a5d666) now stand alone.
